findings.title: canManage() grants management of all groups to admins holding only the VIEW scope
findings.body: `GroupPermissionsV2.canManage()` returns true when the caller has either `VIEW` or `MANAGE` on the all-groups ("Groups") resource: `return hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE);`. `canManage()` is the gate used by `GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup()` (`auth.groups().requireManage()`), so an admin who was only granted view access to all groups can create top-level groups in the realm. This is a privilege escalation relative to the intended V2 scope model (compare `canManage(GroupModel)` in the same class, which correctly checks only `MANAGE`, and `UserPermissions.canManage()` which checks only `MANAGE`). The interface Javadoc in `GroupPermissionEvaluator.canManage()` ("For V2 only: Also if it has permission to VIEW or MANAGE groups") codifies the same mistake. The scope list should be `AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE` only, and the Javadoc fixed accordingly.

findings.title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() returns authz resource IDs instead of group IDs and evaluates the wrong resource
findings.body: In V2 a group's authz `Resource` is created with the group id as its *name* (`AdminPermissionsSchema.resolveGroup` returns `group.getId()` and `getOrCreateResource` calls `resourceStore.create(resourceServer, name, ...)`), and no `setType(...)` is ever called on it. `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` nevertheless (a) iterates `resourceStore.findByType(server, "Groups", ...)`, which only matches the single all-groups resource created in `init()` (the only one with a type), never individual group resources; (b) calls `hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), ...)`, which does `resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId)` with a resource UUID, so the lookup always misses and silently falls back to evaluating the all-groups resource; and (c) adds `groupResource.getId()` (the authz resource UUID) to the result rather than the group id (`getName()`). Consequence: the method either returns an empty set (no per-group restriction ever applied) or, when an all-groups VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS permission exists, returns a set containing a UUID that is not a group. Callers in `UsersResource.searchForUser`/`getUsersCount` and `BruteForceUsersResource.searchForUser` then set `UserModel.GROUPS` to that bogus id, so user search/count is restricted to a non-existent group and returns 0 results for an admin who should see all group members. The current tests do not exercise this path (they only grant VIEW_MEMBERS on a single group, where the evaluator falls back to per-user `canViewByGroup`). The method should use `groupResource.getName()` for both the permission check and the returned id, skip the all-groups resource itself, and the individual resources need a type set (or a different lookup) for `findByType` to find them.

findings.title: NPE when the Groups resource-type resource cannot be resolved
findings.body: `AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(...)` returns `null` when `supportsAuthorizationSchema` is false (e.g. the realm has an admin-permissions client but `adminPermissionsEnabled` was later switched off) or when the "Groups" resource is missing. `hasPermission` immediately passes that value to `policyStore.findByResource(server, resource)` and later `resource.getScopes()`, producing a `NullPointerException` (HTTP 500) on every group endpoint for any admin without the `manage-users`/`view-users` roles. A null check returning `false` is needed before the fallback lookup.

findings.title: requireManageMembers Javadoc references the wrong method
findings.body: The Javadoc for `requireManageMembers(GroupModel)` says "Throws ForbiddenException if {@link #canManageMembership(GroupModel)} returns false", but the implementations throw when `canManageMembers(GroupModel)` returns false (a different scope: `manage-members` vs `manage-membership`). Additionally the Javadoc of `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` says "@return Stream of IDs" while the method returns a `Set<String>`. Since this PR adds the documentation specifically to clarify the scope semantics, these inaccuracies are misleading to implementers.

findings.title: Removal of the global canView() short-circuit causes a policy evaluation per listed group in V2
findings.body: Before this change `getSubGroups` (and `GroupsResource.getGroups`) computed `canViewGlobal = auth.groups().canView()` once and only fell back to `canView(g)` per group. Now `.filter(auth.groups()::canView)` is used directly. In `GroupPermissionsV2.canView(GroupModel)` there is no call to the global `canView()` first; each group triggers `resourceStore.findByName`, a `policyStore.findByResource` lookup and a full policy-engine `evaluatePermission` against the all-groups resource. For an FGAP admin with an all-groups VIEW permission (no `view-users` role) listing N subgroups now costs N policy evaluations instead of one. Either restore the one-time global check in the resources or have `GroupPermissionsV2.canView(GroupModel)` check the all-groups permission once and cache it.

findings.title: No negative test that an all-groups VIEW permission does not grant management, and no test of all-groups VIEW_MEMBERS on user search
findings.body: `testViewGroups` grants the all-groups `VIEW` scope and only asserts that groups become visible; it never asserts that the same admin still cannot create a top-level group or update a group. Such an assertion would have caught `GroupPermissionsV2.canManage()` returning true for `VIEW`. Likewise, none of the tests grant `VIEW_MEMBERS`/`MANAGE_MEMBERS` on the all-groups resource and then search/count users, which is the path that exercises `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` (currently returning authz resource UUIDs instead of group ids and restricting the user search to a non-existent group). Both scenarios should be covered since the PR's purpose is to add the Groups resource type evaluation.

findings.title: getResourceName does not resolve Groups resources, returning null display names
findings.body: `getResourceName` only maps resource names for the `Users` resource type ("All users" / username). Resources created for the new `Groups` type via `getOrCreateResource` are named by the group id and created without a display name, so for group permissions this method falls through to `resource.getDisplayName()` and returns `null` (and the all-groups resource is not mapped to a friendly label either). Any caller rendering permission resources (e.g. admin console listing of permission resources) will show empty/null names for group permissions. A `GROUPS` branch resolving the group (and e.g. "All groups" for the type resource) is needed, mirroring the Users handling.
